title: 'And'/'Or' are non-short-circuiting; porting to C# '&&'/'||' changes evaluation and can hide/expose a NullReference
sourceContent:
Public Class AccessCheck
    Public Function CanEdit(user As User) As Boolean
        ' `And` is NON-short-circuiting: user.HasRole(...) is ALWAYS evaluated,
        ' even when user Is Nothing -> NullReferenceException at runtime.
        ' Ported to C# `&&` (short-circuit) it would NOT throw -> behaviour differs.
        Return user IsNot Nothing And user.HasRole("editor")
    End Function
End Class
notes: VB.NET `And`/`Or` evaluate BOTH operands; `AndAlso`/`OrElse` short-circuit. The guard `user IsNot Nothing And user.HasRole(...)` still dereferences a null user because `And` does not short-circuit — it relies on the exception, or is simply a latent bug. Mechanically translating `And`->`&&` changes semantics (C# `&&` short-circuits). The extractor must flag every `And`/`Or` on booleans and decide whether the intent was short-circuit (`AndAlso`) — usually yes.
